label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 3, pool timeouts 49

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 46 samples; 49 pool acquisition timeouts

report.summary: Transfer failures and slowness coincide with a restart that shrank the DB pool (10→3, timeout 30s→250ms) while an idle-in-transaction session blocked ledger_app sessions. Outbox and consumer look healthy.

findings.claim: Transfers show 28.9% server errors (82×500, 29×503) with p95 2.4s and p99 4.3s.
findings.reason: Request metrics show the error ratio and the latency tail.

findings.claim: A restart at 15:44:37 cut poolMaximumSize from 10 to 3 and connection timeout from 30000ms to 250ms.
findings.reason: Config history shows the change; pool metrics show max 3 and a 250ms timeout.

findings.claim: The pool had 49 acquisition timeouts, consistent with the 500/503 errors under the smaller pool.
findings.reason: 49 timeouts is lower than the 111 errors, so pool exhaustion explains only part of them.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction session (54013) blocked 3 ledger_app sessions for up to ~2s, which could hold connections and cause slow requests.
findings.reason: Blocking was seen in 23-32 samples with max wait 1.971s.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery and the consumer are healthy and not the source of the slowness.
findings.reason: 271 deliveries all succeeded in ~71ms with 0 failed and a max pending age of 3.8s.

limitations: The 500s are not broken down by cause (pool timeout vs. lock wait vs. other); 49 timeouts do not account for 111 errors.
Blocker sampling is every 2s and pool gauges every 5s, and the source of session 54013 is unknown.
next_checks: Identify what owns session 54013 (role 'other') and why it is idle in transaction.
Revert the pool to 10/30000ms and see whether errors drop; check the application error logs for the 500 causes.

alternatives.reason: Blocking began at 15:44:40, right after the restart, so the two causes cannot be separated.
alternatives.hypothesis: The idle-in-transaction blocker alone causes the slow requests and pool starvation, independent of the config change.

alternatives.reason: All deliveries succeeded quickly and none failed.
alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox or consumer delivery problems cause the failures.

report.summary: After the 15:44:37 restart the pool shrank to 3 connections with a 250 ms timeout, and a lock-holding idle-in-transaction session blocked others. Together these likely cause the 500/503s and slow transfers.

findings.claim: Transfers show 29% server errors (82×500, 29×503) with p95 2.4 s and p99 4.3 s.
findings.reason: Request metrics are complete and show the symptom directly.

findings.claim: The restart at 15:44:37 cut the pool max from 10 to 3 and the connection timeout from 30 s to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed settings at the restart inside the window.

findings.claim: The pool hit its limit: 49 acquisition timeouts, active connections up to 3, and max acquire time 260 ms (above the 250 ms timeout).
findings.reason: The timeouts match the new 3-connection, 250 ms configuration.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction session (54013) blocked 3 ledger_app sessions for up to ~2 s. Blocked sessions holding connections starve a 3-connection pool, giving timeouts and slow requests.
findings.reason: The blocking window (15:44:40–15:46:12) overlaps the post-restart errors, but no per-request link is shown.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery is healthy: 271 of 271 attempts succeeded in ~71 ms, with no failures and publications matching arrivals.
findings.reason: The consumer is not the cause.

limitations: Blocking is sampled every 2 s, and the pool pending gauge every 5 s, so short events can be missed.
There are no error logs or traces tying specific 500/503 responses to pool timeouts or the blocking session.
next_checks: Identify what session 54013 is (its query and application) and why it sits idle in a transaction.
Correlate the 500/503 timestamps with the pool timeouts, and re-test with the original pool settings (10 / 30 s).

alternatives.reason: Pool pending was above zero in only 1 of 30 scrapes, so the blocker likely held connections, but the two cannot be separated.
alternatives.hypothesis: Pool undersizing alone, without the lock blocker, explains the errors.
Slow or failing outbox delivery causes the slow transfers.
